LEILA, CHEL URGE SUSTAINED ACTION, INDEPENDENT ANTI-CORRUPTION BODY AT RALLIES

House Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima and House Assistant Minority Leader Chel Diokno on Sunday addressed thousands at separate anti-corruption rallies — De Lima at Luneta and Diokno at the EDSA People Power Monument — urging sustained, peaceful public action and pushing for an independent commission to investigate alleged infrastructure corruption.

De Lima denounced what she called brazen theft tied to flood control projects and urged citizens to maintain pressure through legal action and civic mobilization.

"Magandang araw po sa lahat except sa mga corrupt at ganid o sugapa sa pera! Hindi sila welcome dito," she said, accusing alleged perpetrators of enjoying ill-gotten wealth while ordinary Filipinos suffer.

She called for the passage of the Independent Commission Against Infrastructure Corruption (House Bill No. 4453) and asked the President to certify the measure as urgent, telling protesters to channel their anger into lawful demands for justice.

"Pakiusap ko lang po: Pag-alabin natin ang ating galit hindi para humantong sa dahas o karahasan, kundi para sa pananaig ng hustisya at batas," De Lima said, adding that those responsible must be pursued and punished through the courts.

At EDSA, Diokno said the visible corruption uncovered so far is only a fraction of what he believes was taken, citing estimates that place flood control projects at ₱500 billion and saying the true amount could reach ₱1 trillion. He outlined Akbayan's four demands: open the bicameral committee (bicam) probe, make lawmakers' Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth public, pass House Bill 4453 to give teeth to the proposed independent commission, and prosecute and jail those found culpable.

"Higit sa lahat, ikulong na 'yang mga 'yan! Mabuhay ang sambayanang Pilipino!" Diokno declared.

Both lawmakers stressed peaceful protest, the rule of law, and continued civic vigilance as the nation presses for accountability amid the ongoing flood control investigations.

TRAFFIC PLAN & ADVISORY FOR  22-09-2025:- 
NH-44 (NHW)
Jammu-Srinagar NHW (NH-44) has NOT been fully restored at Tharad, Udhampur. 

There was very slow movement observed on NH-44 due to single lane traffic, undulating & uneven surface of the road at Tharad, breakdown of 03 HMVs and 12 nomadic flocks.   

Traffic managed on regulated manner at Tharad, Udhampur on NH-44 due to single lane about 250-300 Mtrs.

 Commuters are advised to follow lane discipline; overtaking, wrong lane driving will cause congestion. Avoid travel on NH-44, if not necessary.

Subject to fair weather and good road condition, tomorrow only one way traffic for LMVs shall be permitted from Srinagar towards Jammu on  NH-44.

These vehicles shall be allowed from NAVYUG Tunnel  (Qazigund side) between 0700 hrs to 1000 hrs

No LMV/HMV shall be allowed from Jammu towards Srinagar on NH-44. 

LMVs going towards Distt. Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban from Jammu shall be allowed from Nagrota (Jammu) between 0700 hrs 1000 hrs.  However, LMVs/HMVs coming from Distt. Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban towards Jammu  will be permitted to move but these vehicle must cross the Nashri Tunnel before 1000 hrs.

Mughal road is open for LMVs from Jammu towards Srinagar  and vice versa. 

HMVs/Load Carriers:- 
Subject to fair weather and better road conditions, HMVs shall be allowed from NAVYUG Tunnel (Qazigund side) towards Jammu after assessing the traffic situation and road condition on NH-44.  TCU Srinagar shall liaise with TCU Ramban before releasing the HMVs. 

SFs Convoy Movement:-
Security Forces are advised/requested not to ply against advisory /traffic plan in view of possible traffic congestion because of narrow carriage way between Tharad and Balinallah/Marog and Kishtwar Pathar on Jammu-Srinagar NHW. Tomorrow they may ply from Srinagar towards Jammu after confirming the status of NHW from TCU Ramban.

Kishtwar- Sinthan- Anantnag NH-244:- 
Subject to fair weather and good road condition, after getting green signal from NHIDCL, only LMVs shall be allowed from both sides viz from Anantnag towards Kishtwar and vice- versa on Kishtwar-Sinthan-Anantnag road. These vehicles shall be allowed from PP Parana towards Anantnag from 0800 hrs to 1500 hrs and from PP Daksum towards Kishtwar from 0900 hrs. to 1500 hrs. as per order issued by SDM Chhatroo vide No. SDM/C/2025-26/530-37 dated 15-09-2025 and SDM Kokernag vide No. SDM/KNG/665-71 dated 16-05-2025.     

SSG ROAD  
Subject to fair weather and good road condition, (after getting green signal from the BRO) traffic movement shall be allowed on regulated manner on Srinagar-Sonamarg-Gumari road. LMVs followed by HMVs shall be allowed from Minamarg towards Srinagar at 0500 hrs. to 1000 hrs. Similarly, LMVs followed by HMVs shall be allowed from Sonamarg towards Kargil at 1130 hrs to 1730 hrs . No vehicle shall be allowed after cut off timing. 
SFs Convoy, plying from Srinagar to Kargil and vice versa shall plan their movement in such a manner so that Civil Traffic (both UP and DOWN) don't get disturbed.

Mughal Road:- 
Subject to fair weather and good road condition, after getting green signal from Road maintenance agencies (GREF). LMVs Passenger/Private Cars shall be allowed from both sides viz Jammu towards Srinagar and vice versa via Poonch. These vehicles shall be allowed from Behramgala (Baffliaz) between 0600 hrs. to 1730 hrs  and from Herpora (shopian) between 0600 hrs and 1700 hrs as per advisory issued by District Magistrate Poonch vide  No. DMP/J/9291-9318 dated 31-08-2025. However, HMVs carrying essential commodities six tyres only shall be allowed from Poonch towards Shopian and No HMV shall be allowed after 0900 hrs. from Akhnoor Naka. Moreover, No HMV will be allowed from Herpora Naka towards Mughal road . TCU Jammu and TCU Srinagar will inform all concerned about the traffic advisory and cut off timings.

I’ve always chosen to stand up for what I believe is right. I was there at the Never Again rally in EDSA when Marcos Sr. was allowed to be buried at the Libingan ng mga Bayani. I joined rallies in Antipolo, Makati, and Ateneo during Leni’s campaign (I couldn’t be in Pasig because I wasn’t in the Philippines then). Today, I happen to be away again, so I couldn’t be there in person but my heart stands with you.

This is not about colors or sides. This is about fairness, honesty, and the kind of country we all deserve. We must never stop holding our government accountable. Remember this feeling, and don’t let it fade until real change happens.

Hanggang dulo, patuloy pa ring titindig para sa tama, para sa totoo, at para sa bawat Pilipino. 

Ang namulat, hindi na muling mapipikit.

The Philippine capital saw its largest protest in years with the “Trillion Peso March.”

More than 80,000 people — mostly students and activists — accused authorities of stealing funds earmarked for flood relief. The money vanished, while disaster damage remains unaddressed.

Protesters burned tires, threw stones and bottles, and stormed government buildings. Around 40 police officers were injured, and 17 people were arrested.

According to The Guardian, as much as $17.6 billion may have been stolen. Viral footage shows the lavish homes of officials.

The finance minister previously admitted corruption “eats up” to 70% of infrastructure funds. Protesters demand asset disclosures from officials and warn of new rallies if the government stays silent.

Sa ika-53 anibersaryo ng deklarasyon ng Batas Militar, kinalampag ng nagsanib-puwersang taumbayan ang iba-ibang dako ng Metro Manila bilang paniningil sa nagpapatuloy na katiwalian at karahasan mula pa noong diktadura ng ama ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Dumaluyong mula UP Diliman ang mga miyembro ng komunidad patungong Luneta, kung saan naitala ang mahigit 80,000 kataong kumilos upang kondenahin ang talamak na pandarambong at pagkitil sa karapatan sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos-Duterte.

Giit ni Rep. Sarah Elago ng Gabriela Women’s Party, kailangang patuloy na magkaisa at kumilos ang mamamayan sa harap ng tumitinding krisis ng katiwalian. “Hindi lang tayo matututo mula sa kasaysayan kundi ang sambayanang Pilipino ay handa ring gumawa ng kasaysayan,” ani Elago. “Kasaysayan ng paglaban, kasaysayan ng pagkakaisa, kasaysayan na dapat nang baguhin ang bulok na sistema.”

Upang ipagpatuloy ang pagkilos pagkatapos ng Baha sa Luneta, nagtungo ang taumbayan sa Mendiola kung saan naghihintay ang barikada ng armadong kapulisan. Tahasang ginamit ng mga pulis ang kanilang puwersa upang marahas na i-disperse ang mga dumalo.

Pinuno naman ng nagkaisang grupo ng mamamayan, katuwang ang simbahan, ang kahabaan ng EDSA-Ortigas para sa Trillion Peso March. Bitbit ang panawagan kontra korapsiyon, sinasalamin ng martsa ng 100,000 mamamayan ang People Power Revolution na nagpatalsik sa diktadurang Marcos.
